text:
izzy_support: Hey team — customer jane reported we didn't open a support case for a billing outage; instead the system created an ops log entry. Can someone check autorouter logs?

customer_jane: @izzy_support here's the timeline — 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC I hit the support widget, provided order_id and described the billing charge. No case number, only a log id was returned. Very urgent.

izzy_support: Repro steps from their payload attached: 
```json
{
  "user_id": "acct_9876",
  "intent": "report_billing_issue",
  "order_id": "ord_55f9",
  "notes": "customer charged twice",
  "source": "widget"
}
```

marc_sre: grabbing logs now. saw an autorouter decision where two tools matched: ops/log_entry (score 0.77) and support/create_case (score 0.75) and it picked ops/log_entry. Looks like tie-break favors ops.

marc_sre: snippet from decision log:
```json
{"matched_tools": ["ops/log_entry","support/create_case"], "scores": {"ops/log_entry": 0.77, "support/create_case": 0.75}, "selected": "ops/log_entry", "selector_version": "v2.4.1"}
```

izzy_support: ugh. So the customer got only a log id; no SLA, no case tracking. This caused them to miss our SLO. We need a fix and a repro for the eng team.

tina_product: FYI we shipped a change last week that added a freeform "notes" field to ops/log_entry to capture quick telemetry. Might have increased overlap. @marc_sre could that explain the score bump?

marc_sre: yes, the new signature for ops/log_entry now accepts (user_id, source, notes) where notes is untyped string. That makes fuzzy matcher treat consumer payload as matching ops/log_entry more often. support/create_case requires (user_id, issue_type, order_id) but our classifier didn't see explicit issue_type so scores were close.

dev-bot: New insight from selector eval: when payload contains order_id AND phrase "billing" or "charge", support/create_case should get +0.1 boost. Current model rule-set doesn't include those heuristics.

izzy_support: Repro script (quick):
1) POST /router/invoke payload as above
2) expect support/create_case route and case_id in response.

marc_sre: Proposed mitigation: temporarily increase priority weight for support/create_case in selector config and add an explicit rule: if order_id present => prefer support/create_case. I'll push a config rollback to selector-priority v2.4.2.

tina_product: Also should we add explicit schema constraints so ops/log_entry wont accept order_id? That would reduce accidental matches. Ops agreed?

opsbot: CI check: selector-priority change safe? - running integration tests... all green.

marc_sre: Deployed selector-priority v2.4.2 (hotfix). Decision logs now show support/create_case score boosted and selected. Example after fix:
```json
{"matched_tools": ["support/create_case","ops/log_entry"], "scores": {"support/create_case": 0.85, "ops/log_entry": 0.72}, "selected": "support/create_case", "selector_version": "v2.4.2"}
```

izzy_support: Can someone ping the customer and trigger the widget again? I want to confirm they now get a case id. @customer_jane can you retry?

customer_jane: retried at 2026-03-15 10:03 UTC — got case_id CASE-2026-314. Thanks, much better.

izzy_support: great. Root cause summary for the ticket: schema overlap after ops/log_entry signature became more permissive. Selector ML model ties and priority favored ops/log_entry. Fixes: (1) hotfix priority bump for support/create_case (deployed v2.4.2) (2) follow-up: tighten ops/log_entry schema to reject order_id and add unit tests for selector heuristics (ticket INF-493).

tina_product: I'll author the product acceptance criteria for INF-493; assign to eng-ml and eng-platform.

marc_sre: adding tests to prevent regressions. Also recommend adding a fallback confirmation step in widget: "We will create a support case unless you only want to log a note" to reduce ambiguity.

izzy_support: thanks everyone — closing thread once INF-493 is triaged. :white_check_mark:
